sources: Monterey Bay Aquarium, Sea otter: the densest fur of any animal, up to about a million hairs per square inch; no blubber, they stay warm with fur and trapped air and must groom constantly; they eat about a quarter of their body weight a day; they use rocks as tools to crack open shellfish while floating on their backs; a loose pouch of skin under each forearm stores food and a favourite rock; they wrap themselves in kelp to keep from drifting while they sleep, and groups resting together are called rafts; mothers carry pups on their chests and pups' fluffy fur keeps them afloat; https://www.montereybayaquarium.org/animals/animals-a-to-z/sea-otter

US Fish & Wildlife Service / NOAA, Southern sea otter: a keystone species, eating sea urchins that would otherwise overgraze kelp forests; https://www.fws.gov/species/southern-sea-otter-enhydra-lutris-nereis

title: Sea Otters Have a Skin Pocket for Their Favorite Rock 🦦
tiktok_caption: sea otters keep their favorite rock in a skin pocket under their arm 🦦 and they have the thickest fur of any animal. Would you share your snacks with one? 🐚 yes / 🙅 mine #meatballmyths #learnontiktok #seaotter #animalfacts

beats.say: Under its arm, it keeps a pocket for its favorite rock.
It floats on its back, belly up, all day.
The sea otter. Whiskers, paws, and a rock in its pocket.
It dives down and grabs a clam.
Then it pounds the shell on its rock, until it cracks.
The rock goes back in the pocket, for next time.
It has no blubber, so the cold sea is a real danger.
Its fur is the thickest of any animal on Earth.
A rock in its pocket, and up to a million hairs per square inch.
